hypotheses.hypothesis: The checkout error is directly tied to failed requests in the `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` span, as it shows a consistent count of 2 erroneous calls from 07:00Z to 07:20Z.
hypotheses.predicts: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", span_name="oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) > 0 unless on() sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", span_name="oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m] offset 10m)) > 0
hypotheses.evidence: At 07:11:00Z checkout's PlaceOrder SERVER spans failed at 0.0082/s (about 6 % of 0.133 orders/s), and the same window 10 minutes earlier (06:56-07:01) had no failed PlaceOrder at all, so the `unless` part is empty and the query returns 0.0082. At the baseline 07:00:45Z the query returns nothing. The component is right (checkout's PlaceOrder really failed), but the time is wrong: the agent read the raw counter value 2 as a constant error rate 'from 07:00Z', while the error series only appears after the 07:05:45Z onset. The agent also went no further than the page itself, which already said checkout errors.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The error originates from downstream failures in `oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct`, which may be causing the checkout service to fail during order placement.
hypotheses.predicts: sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="product-catalog", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER", span_name="oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) > 0.05 and on() sum(rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="checkout", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT", span_name="oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])) > 0
hypotheses.evidence: At 07:11:00Z product-catalog answered GetProduct with errors at 0.149/s on its own SERVER spans, and checkout's CLIENT GetProduct calls failed at 0.0082/s, the same rate as checkout's failed PlaceOrder: the failure is downstream in product-catalog and propagates into order placement. At the baseline 07:00:45Z neither error series exists, so the query returns nothing. This goes beyond the page: the agent found the failing dependency.

hypotheses.hypothesis: The error is likely propagated from a failing `PaymentService/Charge` step in the checkout flow, as payment failures commonly cause user checkout errors.
hypotheses.evidence: At 07:11:00Z payment served 0.125 Charge requests/s and its only STATUS_CODE_ERROR series (a flagd EventStream client span, which exists in the snapshot) has a rate of 0, so the comparison returns nothing. Checkout's only failing client call is GetProduct (0.0082/s); there is no failed Charge anywhere. The agent offered this from general knowledge ('payment failures commonly cause') and never queried payment.

hypotheses.hypothesis: A system-wide spike in errors could be due to high load or a resource bottleneck, inferred from the error counts growing steadily over the 20-minute window.
hypotheses.evidence: Load did not rise: all SERVER spans ran at 15.79/s at 07:11:00Z against 16.11/s ten minutes earlier (no 20 % increase). The errors were not system-wide: only 4 services had failing SERVER spans (product-catalog, checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy), all on the GetProduct path, so the count is not above 5. Both parts of the disjunction return nothing. The 'growing steadily' premise is also false in the agent's own tool result, where the counter stays at 2.
